The graph above shows a portion of the curve $y=2\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=2\sqrt{3}.$
Find an expression of the form
$x=\theta +n\cdot b,$
where $\theta \in [0,\pi ),$ $n$ is an integer and $b$ is the period in radians, that generates the $x$-coordinates of the points of intersection.

{{field-1}}

feedback.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{tan}⁡x=2\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡x=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

The tangent function has a period of $\pi .$  Hence, the general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{3}+n\cdot \pi .
$$
